title: Legal Assessment
subtitle: Professional expert opinions, legal memoranda, and positions of human rights bodies.
intro: This section consolidates the intellectual foundation of the defense. Here you will find documents confirming the groundlessness of the prosecution from the perspective of international law, fundamental human rights, and enforceable arbitration rulings.

sections.title: Serbian Defense (Extradition Proceedings)
sections.content: Procedural documents and memoranda submitted to Belgrade courts.
sections.summary: Legal documentation of the commercial nature of the conflict. The defense consistently demonstrates that the extradition request is based on a transaction whose legality has been confirmed by arbitration rulings. This is a legal barrier against the attempt to criminalize civil relations.

sections.title: Human Rights Framework
sections.content: Conclusions and positions of independent institutions on the risks of arbitrary prosecution.
sections.summary: Classification of the case as one that violates fair justice standards. Human rights advocates analyze the disproportionality of the criminal pressure and point to the use of the law enforcement system in the interests of parties to a corporate conflict.

sections.title: Professional Legal Expertise
sections.content: Analytical notes, expert opinions, and memoranda from international lawyers.
sections.summary: Detailed analysis of the legal contradictions in the case. Experts analyze the absence of corpus delicti, the insolvency of charges of 'conspiracy,' and the legal consequences of ignoring arbitration rulings in criminal proceedings.

summary: This section presents the consolidated position of leading legal experts. Here you will find the arguments proving the need to return the case to the legal field and to end the unlawful prosecution.
